rows.description: A toddler who answers after a long delay is often processing, not ignoring. Adults who wait a few seconds after asking a question give a small child room to respond.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler talks over others because turn-taking is not yet formed, not because of rudeness. Adults model brief pauses and say your turn, my turn to build the habit.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler settles to a caregiver's lullaby because the slow rhythm, warm voice and closeness signal safety. The soothing effect comes more from the relationship and rhythm than from the tune itself.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler hums, coos and sings wordless melodies while playing, showing contentment and self-soothing. Adults who echo the tune build connection and early language rhythm.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler at drop-off may cry, cling or wave in turns as goodbye feelings mix. A short, predictable farewell ritual helps regulate distress better than sneaking away.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler waves, says bye-bye or babbles hello to show recognition and social interest. Shyness may lead to hiding instead, so adults do not force a greeting.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler lights up, reaches or toddles toward a returning caregiver. This welcoming display shows secure attachment and joy, and predictable goodbyes and reunions strengthen it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler points and names objects, sharing attention and information about what is interesting. Adults who respond by naming back build vocabulary and the sense that sharing matters.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler asks what-that with rising tone or a pointing gesture, seeking names and attention. The question is often social as much as informational, so an answer plus a smile is enough.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler shows recognition of a familiar person with a smile, reaching or excited sounds. Absence of recognition around strangers can appear as staring or turning away.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
